_about: crypto-trader-skill settings. Copy to crypto/config.json (python3 crypto-setup/setup.py init) and edit. Keys starting with _ are notes.
_data: Where prices come from. auto tries Binance, then Bybit, then Hyperliquid, and keeps the first that answers from your location.
_risk_day: null: the risk day still resets at midnight in display_tz. "UTC": midnight UTC, so Asia/Kuala_Lumpur can be the printed clock without moving the risk day.
_money: Your account and your limits. Every order passes crypto-risk against these before it can go anywhere. max_cost_r: the most fees and slippage may take from a trade that ends at its stop, in R (0.2 is a fifth of the risk; 0 turns the rule off).
_leverage: Leverage and margin. Isolated margin limits a loss to the margin you put up for that one position.
_costs: Fees and slippage in basis points (0.01%). null fees: the venue's base rate. null slippage: measured from the live order book when the plan is made.
_orders: paper true simulates fills at live prices against the real order book. Live orders need paper false, your own keys in environment variables, a PASS from crypto-risk and your typed yes.
_news: null: crypto-news reads its built-in outlets (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, The Block, CryptoSlate, Bitcoin Magazine, BeInCrypto). Or a list of RSS or Atom feed URLs, or [name, url] pairs, to read instead.
_paper_profile: tools/auto_paper.py only: a fresh simulated account. It never places an order. Live orders keep max_daily_loss_usd (30) and max_trades_per_day (4) above, and still need a ticket plus a typed yes. Risk per trade is min(risk_pct of this experiment's equity, max_loss_per_trade_usd).
